speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg started and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and anterior uveitis, this presentation is highly suggestive of an autoimmune process rather than a simple insect bite reaction. I would like to assess your current systemic symptoms and review your medication list. Do you currently have any active gastrointestinal symptoms like diarrhea or abdominal pain, and are you taking any immunosuppressive medications?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of trauma (ant bite) triggering a painful ulcer with purplish borders in a patient with Crohn's disease is classic for pyoderma gangrenosum, but I must rule out infection and vascular causes. Do you have any fever or chills, and have you noticed any purulent discharge from the lesion?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent travel to Wisconsin, I need to rule out Sporotrichosis, which can present as a painful ulcer after an insect bite or plant trauma. Have you had any exposure to hay, sphagnum moss, or rose bushes during your trip, and did the lesion start spreading along your lymphatic channels?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic history of trauma triggering a painful ulcer with purplish borders in a patient with Crohn's disease, pyoderma gangrenosum is the most likely diagnosis. I will request a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
